In this writ petition, the petitioners are assailing the letter dated 15.02.2023 (Annexure-P) issued
by respondent No.2, i

nsofar as imposing the condition to change the revenue records/Akarbandh for sanction of modified development plan by the BDA, inter-alia seeking declaration as sought for in prayer B and C to the writ petition.

The relevant facts for adjudication of the writ petition are that, the petitioners claims to be the absolute owners in possession of the property bearing BBMP Katha No.402/1 to 10 situated at Nagavara village comprising the Site No.1 to 9 (Northern Portion) and 9 (Southern Portion) formed by Vyalikaval House Building Co-operative Society Layout, in Nagavara village, Kasaba Hobli,
Bengaluru North Taluk, now falling within the purview of Ward No.6 of Byatarayanapura Sub-Division, BBMP, Bengaluru.
4.

sentences.text: It is case of the petitioners that, the petitioners had filed an application for development plan under Section 15 of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, for developing the building in the said property and as such, the Bengaluru Development Authority has sanctioned the provisional development plan as per letter dated 26.09.2018 (Annexure-J).

sentences.text: It is also stated by the petitioners that, they had paid necessary fee in respect of the development of the plan dated 07.12.2018 and as NC: 2024:KHC:26729 such, work order was issued as per the letter dated 07.12.2018 (Annexure-K).

In the meanwhile, the project of the petitioners was also approved by the Government as per order dated 08.03.2019 and after approval of the project in the 114th State Level Single Window Clearance Committee (SLSWCC) meeting held on 27.02.2019.

sentences.text: At the time of granting sanction of the development plan, the Bengaluru Development Authority had verified the records pertaining to the land in question / possession and it is further contended that, the compensation was also paid to the Government and requisite fee for conversion of the land is also paid while forming the layout and therefore, it is the contention of the petitioners that, the nature of the land was extinguished by operation of law and there is no B-kharab land insofar as the claim made by the respondents - authorities are concerned.

5. It is also averred in the writ petition that, after the sanction of the development plan, a portion of the land has been acquired by the Government as per the NC: 2024:KHC:26729 provisions under Smt R Sarada @ R Sharadamma vs State Of Karnataka on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63621607/

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners made an application seeking modification of the development plan on account of the acquisition made by the respondents - authorities for acquiring the land for BMRCL.

In this regard, as the subject land was falling within the limits of Ward No.6 of Bytarayanapura Sub Division, BBMP, the application made by the petitioners was considered by the BDA and as such, modified development plan, dated 15.03.2023 vide Annexure-M.
6.
It is also stated that, the BDA had issued a modified work order dated 15.03.2023 (Annexure-N).

After sanctioning the modified development plan, the BDA had imposed a fresh condition as per condition No.2 in Annexure-N, calling upon the petitioners to obtain corrections in the revenue authorities with regard to the B- Karab.

It is the contention of the petitioners that, the said NC:
2024:KHC:26729 condition, would not have been imposed by the BDA vide Annexure-H and it is further stated that the fresh condition is solely on account of the order passed by Respondent No.2 and therefore, it is contended in the writ petition that, the impugned letter dated 15.02.2023 (Annexure-P) issued by respondent No.2 imposing condition to change the revenue records/Akarbandh at this length of time, as the land itself is within purview of the BBMP and the same is liable to be interfered with in this petition.
Hence, this petition is filed.

7. Heard the learned counsel appears for the petitioners and learned Additional Government Pleader for the respondents and perused the material on record.
8.

It is contended by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that, as the kharab land has been acquired pursuant to the final notification passed under the provisions of the KIAD Act, as well as a portion of the land has been acquired by the KIDB under the provisions of the Karnataka Industrial Development Act for NC: 2024:KHC:26729 the benefit of the BMRCL, the said aspect ought to have been considered by the respondent - authorities, particularly respondent No.2 while addressing the letter at Annexure-P to the writ petition.

sentences.text: It is also contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner by referring to Annexure-J, dated 26.09.2018 that, the requisite fee has been made in terms of the sanction plan made by the BDA and further the compensation has been paid to the Government in this regard and at this juncture, respondnet No.2 ought not to have issued the letter at Annexure-P, seeking for correction of the revenue records/Akarbandh.
Accordingly, sought for allowing the petition.

9. In this regard, the learned counsel for the petitioners refers to the judgment of this Court in the case J.M.Narayana and Others Vs Corporation of the City of Bangalore, By its Commissioner Office,
Bangalore and Others reported in ILR 2005 KAR 60, and Order dated 10.02.2012 passed in WP No.44277/2011 in the NC: 2024:KHC:26729 case of Sobha Developers Limited Vs Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike and in the case of Hewlett Packard (India) Software Operation Private Limited Vs Tashildhar-Bangalore East Taluk Office, in WP No.209/2020 disposed of on 01.09.2020 and argued that, respondent No.2 has no jurisdiction for change of the Akarbandh as well as sanction plan of the land in question that has been converted as it is situate within the purview of the BBMP jurisdiction.

It is also not in dispute that a portion of the property bearing Survey No.103/06, measuring to an extent of 0-08 guntas out of 0-29 guntas which was conveyed by M/s Manyata Promoters Private Limited in favour of one Sri E.Muralidhar and E.Venkat Reddy as per Sale Deed dated 03.05.2010 and the Eastern road was not shown in the said Sale Deed and the rectification was made as per Annexure-U to the writ petition.

In that view of the - 12 - Smt R Sarada @ R Sharadamma vs State Of Karnataka on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63621607/

sentences.text:
15. In this backdrop of the matter, the Division Bench of this Court in the case of J.M.Narayana (supra) at paragraph No.5, held as follows:
"We have given our anxious consideration to the submissions made at the Bar.
It is not disputed that the suit property stands included within the Corporation limits in terms of a notification issued much earlier to the filing of the suit.

As a result of such inclusion, the taxes applicable within the Corporation limits would by operation of law and in particular Section 4 sub-section 4 of the Municipal Corporation Act become applicable to the extended area also.

Even assuming that the land in question was agricultural land before its inclusion in the Corporation limits, the same would not necessarily mean that it either continued to pay land revenue nor would such land be exempted from payment of property tax under the said Act.

As rightly pointed out by Mrs.Patil, Section 110 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporation Act,
1976, exempts the payment of property tax qua only such lands as are registered to be agricultural lands in revenue records of Government and as are actually used for cultivation of crops.

Stated Conversely just because certain land included in the Corporation limits is registered or used for cultivation purposes would not imply that the said land continues to pay land revenue under the Land Revenue Act.
On the contrary, Land revenue Act would cease to be applicable no sooner the land is brought within the Corporation limits."

The Division Bench of this Court in the case of M.Muninarayana Swamy and Another Vs State of Karnataka and Others reported in ILR 2012 KAR 3428 at paragraph No.3 held as follows:
"3. It is not in dispute that lands are situated in Ward No.9 of Chikkaballapur Town and when the property situated within the Town Municipal Council area when Town Municipal Council has collected development charges from the appellants and granted plan for construction of the compound and in the planning area if it has lost the character of agriculture

entities.text: M.Muninarayana Swamy and Another Vs State of Karnataka and Others reported in ILR 2012 KAR 3428

sentences.text: , the Dy. Commissioner will not get any right to cancel the khata on the ground that the appellants have not obtained an order of conversion.

Therefore, we are of the opinion that there is no necessity for the appellants to obtain conversion from agriculture to non-agriculture, if the area comes within the Town Municipal council limits and in the background of Town Municipal Council collecting the developmental charges and treated as Municipal property."

It is also not in dispute that Sobha Developers Limited supra paragraph No.20 and 21 held as follows:
"20.
Petitioner has produced along with the rejoinder filed on 22.11.2011, a Revised Master plan 2015, and the proposed land use map in respect of the area in question.
The drain passing in the lands in question is indicated with two parallel green lines under the category Hydrography.
The area earmarked in purple colour is shown as industrial area, whereas the area shown in yellow colour is the residential area.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner has got the area that was earlier reserved for industrial purpose changed into residential purpose.

It is also not in dispute that as per the Master - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:26729 Plan, its construction is in the area meant for residential purpose including the portion for which the petitioner got the change of land use from industrial to residential purpose.
Admittedly, there is no other drain, nala or pathway in the Master Plan to demonstrate that the petitioner had deviated the same for the purpose of putting up construction.

It is also evident from Annexure-C - survey sketch prepared by the BDA on 03.03.2006 that no Nala or pathway as claimed by the respondent-Corporation has been shown to be running in the lands in question as is sought to be projected in the survey sketch prepared by the Surveyor based on the village map.
Annexure-C - Sketch prepared by the BDA is prior to the date on which the petitioner was granted license.

21. As rightly contended by the Counsel for the petitioner, once the Master Plan is prepared indicating the existence of roads, drains, streets etc., and particularly the Planning Authority at an undisputed point of time had prepared a sketch of the lands wherein no such passage of Nala in the middle of the property or the existence of pathway therein was shown, it is not open for the Corporation at such a belated stage to raise an objection solely based on the village map to contend that the existing Nala was deviated by the petitioner.

It is to be noticed that the draft of the Master Plan would be published and sent to the Government enclosing the report of the survey conducted and after taking into consideration all the relevant aspects, the Master Plan submitted by the Planning Authority viz., BDA for approval and the same is approved.
The BBMP, at no stage had raised any objection nor is there anything to show that anybody had raised any objection to the contents of the revised Master Plan when the objections were called for.
The Revised Master Plan 2015 has come into effect on 25.06.2007.

The Master Plan contains showing of lands, street pattern,
areas reserved for parks, playgrounds and other civic amenities or for public purpose as also areas of special control and development.
In such circumstances the objection raised by the Corporation at the stage of grant of underground cable connection to the occupants of the premises is wholly unjustified.

Section 505 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, makes it clear that exercise of powers by the Smt R Sarada @ R Sharadamma vs State Of Karnataka on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63621607/

18. It is also relevant to note that, in the said judgment of this Court, in the case of Hewlett Packard (India) Software Operation Private Limited, wherein paragraph Nos.11 and 20 this Court held as follows:
"11.

entities.text: Hewlett Packard (India) Software Operation Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The question involved in this writ petition is, whether the Tahsildar under the provisions of Karnataka Land Revenue Act can conduct survey and fix the boundaries in respect of land situated within the Corporation limits of Bengaluru.
20. The object of the KLR Act is to regulate the user of land and collect land revenue.
The Division Bench of this Court in the case of J.M.Narayan and others (supra) has held that the KLR Act would cease to the applicable no sooner the land is brought within the corporation limits.

The law laid down in the aforesaid case has been followed by the Division Bench and Coordinate Bench of this court when the question regarding, whether permission of the Deputy Commissioner is required or not under Section 95 of the KLR Act for diverting the lands situated within corporation limits for non- agricultural purposes fell for consideration.

The Division Bench and Co-ordinate Benches following the law laid down in the case of J.M.Narayan (supra)
in unequivocal terms have held that the KLR Act is not applicable to lands situated within corporation limits and as such the permission of the Deputy Commissioner under Section 5 of the KLR Act for diverting the land is not required.

Hence, the submission of the learned Senior counsel appearing for respondent No.2 that the law laid down in the case of J.M.Narayana (supra) is confined to a dispute with regard to the payment of court fee and not relating to other matters to be dealt with under the provisions of - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC:26729 KLR Act is not acceptable.

If the KLR Act ceases to apply to lands falling within the limits of corporation, it is implied that the Tahsildar has no jurisdiction to carry out survey work and fix boundaries in respect of the land in question.
The law laid down in the case of J.M.Narayan and others (supra) which has been followed by this Court in catena of cases is squarely applicable in the case on hand.

Since it is held that the KLR Act is not applicable to the land in question, the other issues regarding jurisdiction of the land in question, the other issues regarding Smt R Sarada @ R Sharadamma vs State Of Karnataka on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63621607/
8 jurisdiction of the Civil Court to decide boundary dispute need not be gone into".

sentences.text: 19. Following declaration of law made by this Court in the aforementioned judgments, wherein, the land Revenue Act ceases to have any application in respect of the lands falling within the limits of Corporation - BBMP and the revenue authorities have no jurisdiction to carry out survey of boundaries in respect of land in question and that too by issuing the impugned letter as per Annexure-P dated 15.02.2023 to the BDA for modification of the development plan is concerned.

It is needless to say that, as the petitioners have already paid the compensation in favour of the Government and Government order has been made in that aspect, as per the demand notice issued,
thereunder, in that view of the matter, any of further - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:26729 action taken by the respondent authorities including the issuance of letter by the statutory authorities dated 15.02.2023 vide Annexure-P is liable to be quashed.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Writ petition is allowed;
ii) Letter dated 15.02.2023 bearing No.LND(N)CR/206/2021-22 (Annexure-P)
passed by the respondent No.2, imposing condition to change the revenue records/akarband for sanction of modify the development plan by the Bangalore Development Authority is hereby quashed.
iii) It is also made clear that, the B-Kharab land measuring 03 guntas in Sy No.87/1,
B-Kharab measuring 02 gunta sys in Sy No. 87/2B and B-Kharab land 0.1 guntas, in Sy No. 103/6 of Nagavara village, Bangalore North Taluk, does not exist as per the survey akarband and - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:26729 village map, produced at Annexure-AF and AK respectively.

iv) Writ of mandamus is issued to respondent Nos. 2 and 6 to effect correction in the RTC extracts in respect of the land bearing Sy No. No.87/1, Sy No.87/2B and Sy No. 103/6 of Nagavara village,
Bangalore North Taluk as non- agricultural kharab under Rule 104 of Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966.
Ordered accordingly.

It is to be noticed that the draft of the Master Plan would be published and sent to the Government enclosing the report of the survey conducted and after taking into consideration all the relevant aspects, the Master Plan submitted by the Planning Authority viz., BDA for approval and the same is approved.
The Master Plan contains showing of lands, street pattern,
areas reserved for parks, playgrounds and other civic amenities or for public purpose as also areas of special control and development.
In such circumstances the objection raised by the Corporation at the stage of grant of underground cable connection to the occupants of the premises is wholly unjustified.
Section 505 of the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976, makes it clear that exercise of powers by the Smt R Sarada @ R Sharadamma vs State Of Karnataka on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63621607/
7 Corporation shall be in - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:26729 conformity with the provisions of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, with regard to any matter relating to land use or development as defined in the explanation to Section 14".
The Division Bench of this Court in the case of J.M.Narayan and others (supra) has held that the KLR Act would cease to the applicable no sooner the land is brought within the corporation limits.
The Division Bench and Co-ordinate Benches following the law laid down in the case of J.M.Narayan (supra)
in unequivocal terms have held that the KLR Act is not applicable to lands situated within corporation limits and as such the permission of the Deputy Commissioner under Section 5 of the KLR Act for diverting the land is not required.
If the KLR Act ceases to apply to lands falling within the limits of corporation, it is implied that the Tahsildar has no jurisdiction to carry out survey work and fix boundaries in respect of the land in question.
The law laid down in the case of J.M.Narayan and others (supra) which has been followed by this Court in catena of cases is squarely applicable in the case on hand.
opennyai_summary.decision:
19. Following declaration of law made by this Court in the aforementioned judgments, wherein, the land Revenue Act ceases to have any application in respect of the lands falling within the limits of Corporation - BBMP and the revenue authorities have no jurisdiction to carry out survey of boundaries in respect of land in question and that too by issuing the impugned letter as per Annexure-P dated 15.02.2023 to the BDA for modification of the development plan is concerned.
It is needless to say that, as the petitioners have already paid the compensation in favour of the Government and Government order has been made in that aspect, as per the demand notice issued,
thereunder, in that view of the matter, any of further - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC:26729 action taken by the respondent authorities including the issuance of letter by the statutory authorities dated 15.02.2023 vide Annexure-P is liable to be quashed.
In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Writ petition is allowed;
ii) Letter dated 15.02.2023 bearing No.LND(N)CR/206/2021-22 (Annexure-P)
passed by the respondent No.2, imposing condition to change the revenue records/akarband for sanction of modify the development plan by the Bangalore Development Authority is hereby quashed.
iii) It is also made clear that, the B-Kharab land measuring 03 guntas in Sy No.87/1,
B-Kharab measuring 02 gunta sys in Sy No. 87/2B and B-Kharab land 0.1 guntas, in Sy No. 103/6 of Nagavara village, Bangalore North Taluk, does not exist as per the survey akarband and - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:26729 village map, produced at Annexure-AF and AK respectively.
iv) Writ of mandamus is issued to respondent Nos. 2 and 6 to effect correction in the RTC extracts in respect of the land bearing Sy No. No.87/1, Sy No.87/2B and Sy No. 103/6 of Nagavara village,
Bangalore North Taluk as non- agricultural kharab under Rule 104 of Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966.
Ordered accordingly.
